milestone: Reader structured article errors and successful empty-page recovery
scenario: A typed article 404 keeps its not-found meaning, while a successful later empty cursor page keeps a previous-page escape and restores the first page through the existing cursor trail.

failure_before_repair.command: cd apps/reader-web && npm test -- --test-name-pattern='later empty page'
failure_before_repair.result: failed: later empty ArticleList rendered no articleListPager despite hasPrev=true

failure_before_repair.command: cd apps/reader-web && npx playwright test e2e/service-worker.smoke.spec.ts -g 'article 404 envelope' --project=chromium
failure_before_repair.result: failed: the real 404 envelope rendered generic load-failure copy instead of article-not-found copy

failure_before_repair.command: cd apps/reader-web && npx playwright test e2e/service-worker.smoke.spec.ts -g 'successful later empty page' --project=chromium
failure_before_repair.result: failed: the pre-repair fixture returned an article for the later cursor, so no successful empty state or previous escape was observable

repair: FocusedArticleScreen now retains ApiError status/code metadata and classifies not-found by status 404 or code not_found, rather than matching message text.
ArticleList now renders its existing pager when a confirmed empty page still has a previous page; first-page empty results remain pager-free.
The local fixture server now exposes a q=empty-page scenario whose second cursor returns HTTP 200 with an empty item list, allowing the browser recovery path to be tested without a real API.

validation.command: cd apps/reader-web && npm test -- --test-name-pattern='(typed not-found|later empty page)'

validation.result: pass: Next.js production build and TypeScript check

validation.command: cd apps/reader-web && READER_E2E_PORT=3015 PLAYWRIGHT_REUSE_SERVER=false npx playwright test e2e/service-worker.smoke.spec.ts -g 'invalid read route|article 404 envelope|successful later empty page|scan mode paging failure|scan mode error offers' --project=chromium

known_limit: Browser evidence uses the local disposable fixture and Chromium only; it does not prove the deployed FastAPI response, real proxy URL limits, native iPhone selection, screen-reader behavior, staging/production auth, or real user data.
